senses.gloss:
पठ् पठ् (probably a denomin. derived from पष्ट for स्पष्ट; cf. पश्य for स्पश्य), i. 1, Par. (in epic poetry also Ātm.)
 1. To speak distinctly, to recite, MBh. 2, 1154.
 2. To invoke, Hariv. 12561.
 3. To read, to study, Man. 4, 98.
 4. To mention, MBh. 3, 1483.
 5. To declare, Suśr. 2, 260, 16.
 6. To learn from (abl.), Bhāg. P. 9, 22, 37.
 --Caus. पाठय,
 1. To teach one to talk, Hit. Pr. d. 43.
 2. To teach one to read, Bhāg. P. 7, 5, 2.
 3. To cause to read, Pañc. 5, 11.
 4. To teach, Bhāg. P. 7, 5, 2. Frequent. पापठ्य, To recite repeatedly, Kathās. 37, 73.
 --With the prep. अनु अनु, To say after one, to repeat, Bhāg. P. 7, 5, 3.
 --With अभि अभि, अभिपठित, Called, named, Suśr. 2, 310, 18.
 --With परि परि,
 1. To mention, MBh. 1, 2020.
 2. To declare, 3, 14192.
 --With प्र प्र, To recite loudly, Hariv. 9591.
 --With सम् [] सम्, To read, Man. 4, 98.
 --Comp.
 --ptcple. of the fut. pass. of the Caus. अ-संपाठ्य, One with whom nobody is allowed to read (or to pray), Man. 9, 238.
पठक पठ् + अक, m. A reader, MBh. 3, 17395.

पाठक पाठक, i. e. पठ् + अक, m.
 1. A student, one who is conversant with a science, Pañc. 165, 2.
 2. A preceptor.
 --Comp.

पठन पठ् + अन, n.
 1. Reciting, Mārk. P. 51, 26.
 2. Reading, Böhtl. Ind. Spr. 664.
पठर्वन् पठर्वन्, m. A proper name, Chr. 297, 17 = Rigv. i. 112, 17.

पाठ पाठ, i. e. पठ् + अ, m.
 1. Reading, recital, Kathās. 2, 36.
 2. A text.
 --Comp.

पाठिन् पाठिन्, i. e. पाठ + इन्, adj.
 1. Having studied, MBh. 5, 1668.
 2. Conversant with.
पाठीन पाठीन, m. A sort of fish, Silurus boalis Ham.
